text.S1: There once was a married man and woman who wished for a child. At length the woman hoped God was about to grant her desire. These people had a little window at the back of their house from which a splendid garden could be seen, which was full of the most beautiful flowers and herbs. It was surrounded by a high wall, which no one dared to pass, because it belonged to an evil enchantress who had great power and was dreaded by all the world.
text.S2: Once upon a time, there was a couple that wished to bear a child. For a long time, the wife felt that God would fulfil her desire to have a baby.The couple’s house had a small window behind which they used to take a peep at their good garden full of beautiful flowers and herbal medicines. The garden was within a high perimeter wall-fence which no person would manage to jump over it in order to enter as it was for a vicious sinful jugglery woman, who was feared by people in the whole world.
text.T1: Nekunani mutu ni musalaa hae ili bao nebanani nyololelo ya kuba ni mwana. Nako yeñwi wa musali aikutwa kuli mwendi mulimu nase alaba tapelo yahae. Batu ba nebanani ka haulo nyana kwa mulaho wa ndu ili kao neka talimezi kwa kasimunyana, moo nekutezi lipalisa zebuheha mane ni milyani. Neipotilohilwe ki limota lelitelele, foo nekusina mutu yoo nalika kufita teñi, bakeñisa kuli neeli la musali wa mabibo amaswe ili yoo nasabiwa ki lifasi kaufela.
text.T2: Ka nako yeñwi nekuna ni muuna ni musalaahae bane baikumbuta kupepa mwana. Ka nako yetelele, wa musali aikutwa kuli inge mwendi Mulimu nataabe aalabile takazo yahae. Batu ba nebana ni kahaulo kwamulaho wa ndu yabona ili mone banangelelanga simu yende hahulu moo nekutezi lipalisa zende mane ni lipalisa za milyani. Nei potolohilwe ki limota lelitelele, lewo nekusina mutu yoo naaka lika kulitula bakeñisa kuli neeli la musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi ili yanaana ni maata yoo nasabiwa ki lifasi kaufela.

text.S1: One day the woman, who was standing by the window and looking down into the garden, which was planted with the most beautiful flower, named Rapunzel. It looked so fresh and so green she wanted it and had the greatest desire to eat it. This desire increased every day, and as she knew that she could not have any, she quietly languished, and looked pale and tired.
text.S2: The other day, the woman stood by the small window observing the good garden in which there was a planted beautiful flower called rapunzel. The flower looked soft and greenish. She had appetite for it and wished to taste it. Her desire to eat that flower inceased by the day. So when she realized that there was no chance of getting it, she became depressed and subsequently was tired, very weak and grey in complexion.
text.T1: Ka zazi leliñwi musali naa yemi kwa lihaulo inge atalimezi kwa simu yene icezwi palisa yende hahulu yene ibizwa Rapunzelu. Nei bonahala ndelumuna ni butala luli mi nai tokwa ni kuba ni takazo ya kuica. Takazo yahae yaekezeha zazi ni zazi mi hase alemuhile kuli hakoni kufumana kabelo kwateñi, aishonda feela ni kufelelwa ki maata, abonahala buseta ni kukatala.
text.T2: Ka zazi leliñwi musali naa yemi kwa lihaulo inge atalimezi kwa simu yene icezwi palisa yende hahulu yene ibizwa Rapunzelu. Nei bonahala ndelumuna ni butala luli mi nai tokwa ni kuba ni takazo ya kuica. Takazo yahae yaekezeha zazi ni zazi mi hase alemuhile kuli haa koni kufumana kabelo kwateñi, aishonda feela ni kufelelwa ki maata, abonahala buseta ni kukatala.

text.S1: She told the man: "If I can't get some of the rapunzel fruits behind our house to eat, I shall die." And the man thought, “I will bring my wife some of the fruits, let it cost what it will”. In the twilight of the evening, he clambered down over the wall into the garden of the evil enchantress, hastily grabbed a handful of rapunzels, and took them back to his wife. The woman made herself a salad of it, and ate it with joy.
text.S2: She informed the husband, “If I do not manage to get a piece of that rapunzel fruit which is planted behind our house in order for me to eat then I will die." The husband thought to himself, “I should bring to my wife a piece of rapunzel fruit despite any calamity that will come our way.” At dusk, the husband climbed and jumped over the the high wall into the garden that belonged to a vicious sinful jugglery woman. He then quickly plucked some rapunzel flowers that filled his hand and took them to his wife. She cooked the flowers nicely and hapilly enjoyed the meal.
text.T1: Abulelela muuna hae: "haiba nisa fumani kabelo kwa palisa yani ya rapunzelu kuli niche, nikashwa." Mi muuna hae aipulelela, "nika tiseza musalaka litolwana, kutahe ñi kapa ñi konji nitise." Manzibuana hakuse kueza kafifi, wa muuna abe apahama fa limota ni kushetumukela mwa ka simunyana ka muloi yoo wa musali ayanga lizoho lelitezi la litolwana zewo ni kuiseza musala hae. Wa musali aikapehela zona hande mi aca katabo luli.
text.T2: Abulelela muunaahae ali, “Haiba nji hanifumani kwa palisa ya rapunzelu yeeli kwamulaho wa ndu yaluna kuli nice kipeto nikashwa." Mi muunaahae aipulelela ali, “Nikatiseza musalaaka kalulo ya litolwana, niha kukataha butaata bufi kapa kutahe ñi.” Manzibuana hakuse kueza kaswalala, wa muuna abe apahama fa limota ni kushetumukela mwa simu ya musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi yoo. Kapilipili, ayanga litolwana za rapunzelu zetezi lizoho ni kuiseza musalaahae. Wa musali aikapehela zona hande ni kuca katabo.

text.S1: She, however, liked it so much so very much, that the next day she longed for it three times as much as before. Her husband must once more descend into the garden. In the gloom of evening, therefore, he let himself down again; but when he had clambered down the wall he was terribly afraid, for he saw the enchantress standing before him.
text.S2: The wife had enjoyed the meal very much, such that the following day she wished that the meal would be three times more than before. She therefore, hoped that the husband would again return to the garden for the same. It was for that reason that at dusk again her husband climbed over the high permeter wall-fence into the garden. However, that time he badly went down the wall-fence to the ground and got scared when he saw a vicious sinful jugglery woman standing before him.
text.T1: Yena, nihakuli cwalo, atabela hahulu-hulu luli, kuli mane zazi lelitatama akupa muuna hae kuli akone kuyo mutiseza litikanyo zetaalu kufita zeo namu tiselize lwapili.Wa muuna nanani kushetumukela mwa ka simunyana kutula limota hape. Nako ya manzibuana, ka cwalo akala musipili wahae hape, kono hase ashetumukile fafasi aba ni sabo yetuna, bakala kuli natilo bona musali wa mabibo amuyemelezi fa pili yahae.
text.T2: Wa musali kacwalo atabela hahulu-hulu sico sewo luli, kuli mane zazi lelitatama aikumbuta kuli kambe sifumaneha halaalu ni kufita pili. Kambe muunaahae hape akone kuyo kena mwa simu. Kacwalo lizazi hase lilikezi muunaahae apahama limota ni kushetumukela mwa simu hape; kono hase ashetumukile limota ka busafa fafasi aba ni sabo yetuna, kakubona musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi amuyemelezi fapili yahae.

text.S1: "How dare you," said the enchantress with a very angry look, "you descended into my garden and stole my rapunzels like a thief? You will suffer for it!" "Ah," answered the man. "Let mercy take the place of justice, I only made up my mind to do it out of necessity. My wife saw your fruits from the window, and felt such a longing for it she would have died if she had not had some."
text.S2: “How can you do such activity without fear?” a physically annoyed vicious sinful jugglery woman asked. “You jumped over the fence down into my garden to steal my rapunzel fruits like a thief! You will suffer for your action!” “Oh!” exclaimed the man. “Let your clemency take effect as necessary. I have just done this because of need for it. My wife noticed the rapunzel fruits though a small window and desired to taste them though a meal. Therefore, if she had not eaten the flowers, she would have died.”
text.T1: "Ukona kueza cwani nto yecwana," Mwa bulela musali wa mabibo ka ponahalo ya bunyemi luli, "Ushetumukezi mwa kasimunyana kaka ni kuuzwa ma rapunzelu aka sina lisholi? Se ukasi nyandela!" "Haa," Mwa alaba wa muuna nyandela. Nikupa kuni utwela makeke luli, nenieza feela taba ye Kakuli kinto ye tokwahala. Mufumahali waka naboni litolwana zamina mwa lihaulo mi satala takazo yetuna kuli ace kwa litolwana ze, haiba asaici kipeto washwa."
text.T2: “Ukona cwañi kueza nto yecwana usasabi,” kwabulela musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi ka ponahalo ya bunyemi hahulu. “Ushetumukezi mwa simu yaaka ni kuuzwa marapunzelu aaka sina lisholi? Seu ezize ukasi nyandela!” “Haa!” kwaalaba muuna. “Mutuhele makeke aange sibaka sa tukelo. Nenieza feela taba ye kakuli ki nto yetokwahala. Mufumahali waaka naa bonezi lipalisa zamina mwa lihaulo mi saaba ni takazo yetuna yakuli ace kwa litolwana ze, kacwalo hane asike aca kwateñi kipeto nakabe ashwile."

text.S1: Then the enchantress allowed her anger to be softened, and said to him, "If the case be as you say, I will allow you to take away with you as much rapunzel as you want, only I make a condition, you must give me the child which your wife will bring into the world. It will be well treated, and I will care for it like a mother." The man, in his terror, consented to everything, and when the woman gave birth the enchantress appeared at once, named the child Rapunzel, and took her away.
text.S2: For that reason, the level of annoyance of a vicious sinful jugglery woman cooled slightly down and asked the man, “If what you are telling me is what is prevailing, I will then allow you to pluck some of my rapunzel flowers as you wish on condition that you will allow me to be the owner of the child your wife will bear for you in this world. The child will be taken care of nicely just like the mother.” Due to his fear, the man accepted what the he was instructed to do. When the wife gave birth, a vicious sinful jugglery woman appeared once to name the baby Rapunzel and off she went with the born baby.
text.T1: Foo cwale bunyemi bwa musali wa mabibo wabe bwa kusufala hanyinyani, mi ali ku muuna, "haiba taba inzi cwalo, nikaku lumelela kuli ukone kuyanga kwa litolwana zaka kuya ka molatela, haiba lubeya tumelelano, ukanifa mwana yoo aka tahisa mufumahali wahao fa lifasi." "Uka babalelwa hande, mi nika muuta inge mahe." Muuna, mwa sabo yahae, alumela zeo neli bulezwi kaufela, mi wa musali hase atisizwe kwa kupulula, musali wa mabibo abe aiponahaza, abeya mwana libizo la Rapunzelu, mi amuunga kuya niyena.
text.T2: Foo cwale bunyemi bwa musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi bwa kusufala hanyinyani mi ali ku muuna, “Haiba nji taba inzi cwalo mou bulelela, nikaku lumeleza kuli uyange kwa litolwana zaaka za rapunzelu ka mou latela, kono ka tumelelano yakuli ulukela kunifa mwana yoo akapepa mufumahali wahao fa lifasi. Uka babalelwa hande ni kumuuta hande inge mahe.” Muuna mwa sabo yahae alumela zewo neli bulezwi kaufela, mi wa musali hase apuluhile, musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi aiponahaza hañwi ni kushumwenena mwana libizo la Rapunzelu, ni kumuunga kuya niyena.

text.S1: Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful child beneath the sun. The enchantress raised her as her daughter but treated her very cruelly. When she was twelve years old, the enchantress locked her in a tower in a forest, which had neither stairs nor doors. At the top was a little window. When the enchantress wanted to climb in, she placed herself under it and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair to me."  Rapunzel had magnificent long hair, and when she heard the voice of the enchantress she let down her braids, winding them round one of the hooks of the window above, and the enchantress climbed up.
text.S2: Rapunzel grew up and became a responsible child on earth. A vicious sinful jugglery woman looked after the child like her own but with hardness of heart. When the child was twelve years old, a vicious sinful jugglery woman locked her up in a tower located in a forest, which had neither a ladder nor an entrance. On top, at the tower was only a window. In case a vicious sinful jugglery woman would like to climb and visit the child, she would hide herself under the tower and call out the child’s name, “Rapunzel! Rapunzel! Drop your hair.” Rapunzel had very long hair. Once she had received such instruction coming from a vicious sinful jugglery woman, she would let down her well plaited hair which she hanged at one of the hooks by the window of the tower on top. The vicious sinful jugglery woman would then use the long hair to climb to the top.
text.T1: Rapunzelu ayo hula kuba mwana yomunde wamusali mwatasa lizazi. Musali wa mabibo amuhulisa inge mwanahae kono amuuta maswe luli ka lunya. Hase ananai lilimo ze lishumi ka zepeli Twelufu, musali wa mabibo abe amukiyela kwa njongonjongo mwa mushitu, ili koo nekusina matulukelo kapa munyako. Kwa halimu nekunani kahaulo kakanyinyani. Haiba musali wa mabibo nabata kupahama kwateni, nayo huweleza mwa kahaulo ona moo ali, "Rapunzelu, Rapunzelu, wisa milili yahao fafasi. Rapunzelu nanani milili yemitelele luli. Mi asautwa feela linzwi la musali wa mabibo nawisanaga milili yahae yeotilwe anze aikolekile kwa lihaulo kwae halimu, mi musali napahama kayona.
text.T2: Rapunzelu ahula kuba mwana yomunde mwatasaa lizazi. Musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi amuhulisa inge mwanaahae kono amuuta ka lunya. Hase ana ni lilimo zelishumi ka zepeli za kupepwa, musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi amukiyela mwa kalani mwa mushitu ili yene isina matulukelo kapa munyako. Kwahalimu nekuna ni kahaulo. Haiba nji musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi naa bata kupahama kwateñi, naayo ikundeka kwataasi a kalani yewo ni kuweleza ali, “Rapunzelu! Rapunzelu! Niwiseze milili yahao.” Rapunzelu naana ni milili yemitelele hahulu. Mi asa utwa feela linzwi la musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi awisa milili yahae yeotilwe anze aikolekile kwa kashuto kakañwi ka lihaulo kwahalimu, mi musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi apahamela kuyona.

text.S1: After a few years locked in this tower, Rapunzel became miserable. She grew tired and bored of being locked away all these years. It came to pass that the King's son rode eartthrough the forest and saw the tower. He heard a song, which was so charming that he stood still and listened. This was Rapunzel, who in her solitude passed her time in letting her sweet voice resound. The King's son wanted to climb up to see her and looked for the door of the tower, but none was to be found. He rode home, but the singing had so deeply touched his heart that every day he went out into the forest alone and listened to it. Once when he was standing behind a tree, he saw the enchantress arrive and he heard how she cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair."
text.S2: After few years in captivity, while leaving in the tower like that, Rapunzel was miserable. She suffered and felt depressed. She was fed up of leaving in a locked up tower in all those years. As time went by, one day a Prince who was ridding his horse in the bush noticed the tower. As he was coming closer to the tower, he heard a voice of a person singing a nice soothing song coming from the tower. He stopped to listen to the song. It was Rapunzel who was singing to console herself in her loneliness just to pass time through her beautiful voice. The Prince then got interested in the song and wished to meet the girl who was singing. He tried to look for access to the tower but in vain. He was touched by the beautiful voice that produced nice melodies as he returned to the palace and made it a habit of visiting the tower site everyday in order to listen to the girl’s songs. One day as the Prince was standing behind a tree, he saw the vicious sinful jugglery woman arriving and how she was calling out to the girl, “Rapunzel! Rapunzel! Drop your hair to me!”
text.T1: Hasamulaho wa lilimolimo anze atamelezwi kwa njongonjongo, Rapunzelu asukuluka. Aikutwa hahulu bulutu ni kukatala kukiyelwa lilimo zeo kaufela. Nako yeñwi mwana mulena wa muuna azamaela mwa mushitu mi abona kandu kao ka kwa njongonjongo. Autwa kapina, kao neeli kakande luli kuli abe ayema ni kuteeleza. Yoo neeli Rapunzelu, yoo mwahala matata ahae nalika katata kutumusa linzwi lahae lelishalula. Mwana mulena nabata kuli apahame mwa kandu kakwa njongonjongo mi akala kubata-bata munyako kono apalelwa kufumana. Akutela kwandu, kono kapina ka munga hahulu maikuto kuli zazi ni zazi nanze ayanga kuyo teeleza. Zazi leliñwi abona musali wa mabibo ataha kwa kandu kao mi ateeleza moo natilo huwelezela, "Rapunzelu, Rapunzelu, posa milili yahao."
text.T2: Kasamulaho wa lilimo-nyana haanze akwalezwi kwa kalani cwalo, Rapunzelu anyanda. Aikutwa hahulu kukatala ni kunyikwa ka kukiyelwa lilimo zewo kaufela. Nako yeñwi hase ifita, mwanaa mulena wa muuna hanze azamaya mwa mushitu apahami pizi abona kalani. Autwa pina yekateleha mi abe ayema ni kuiteeleza. Neeli Rapunzelu yanaa opela, yoo mwabuinosi bwahae naa sinya nako yahae ka kulukutisa linzwi lahae lelishalula. Mwana mulena nabata kuli apahame ayobona musizana yanaa opela. Kacwalo, akala kubata-bata munyako wa kalani kono apalelwa kuufumana. Akutela kwa ndu, haili muopelelo wona wataba pilu yahae kuli mane zazi ni zazi naanze ayanga anoosi mwa mushitu kuyoteeleza muopelelo woo. Nako yeñwi haanze ayemi kwamulaho wa kota, abona musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi haafita ni kuutwa moo natilo huwela haali, “Rapunzelu! Rapunzelu! Niposeze milili yahao.”

text.S1: Rapunzel let down the braids of her hair, and the enchantress climbed up to her. "I will do the same thing," he said, and the next day he went and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down the hair." Immediately the hair fell down and the boy climbed up. At first Rapunzel was terribly frightened, by the man whose eyes she had never yet beheld. The King's son told her that in his heart he could have no rest, until he had saved her from the evil enchantress. Rapunzel lost her fear, and realized now she could escape the evil enchantress. And she said, "I will willingly go away with you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring with you a scarf of silk each time that you come here, and I will weave a ladder with it.”
text.S2: Rapunzel dropped her dredlocked hair for the vicious sinful jugglery woman to use for climbing to where the girl was. “I will also do the same,” the Prince spoke to himself. Therefore, the following day he went into the bush and upon arrival he called out, “Rapunzel! Rapunzel! Drop your dredlocked hair to me.” Once the dredlocked hair reached down, the Prince then used it to climb to the tower. In the firt place, Rapunzel was scared by the Prince’s eyes which she had never seen before since she was born. The Prince informed the girl that he would’nt be at peace of heart if he had not free her from the captive of the vicious sinful jugglery woman. The girl responded, “I would like to go with you but the challenge is that I do not know how to go down from this tower. Therefore, whenever you come here bring with you a nyelone cloth which I will use to make a decending material.”
text.T1: Rapunzelu aposa milili yahae, mi musali yoo apahama kuya kookoo nainzi musizana.  Nikaeza cwalo nina," aipulelela, mi habusa aya ni kuyo huweleza, "Rapunzelu, Rapunzelu, posa milili yahao." Isawa feela milili mucaha apahama. Fapili Rapunzelu nasabile, asabiswa hahulu ki muuna yoo meeto ahae asambabe abone fateni. Mwana amulena atolokela musizana kuli mwapilu yahae uikonkile kuli hana kuba ni kozo kufitela aka pulusa musizana kwa mazoho a musali wa mabibo a buloi. Mi musizana ali, "Ka tato yaka nikaya niwena, kono hanizibi mwa kutulukela. Utahange ni muhala wa bwanda nako ni nako hautaha kwanu, mi nikakwan luka mutano kawona."
text.T2: Rapunzelu amuposeza milili yahae yeotilwe, mi musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi yoo apahama kuya koo nainzi musizana. “Nikaeza cwalo nina,” aipulelela. Cwale habusa aya kwateñ ni kuyohuweleza ali, "Rapunzelu! Rapunzelu! Niposeze milili yahao.” Milili isawela feela fafasi, mucaha ni yena apahama kalani. Fapili Rapunzelu naa sabisizwe hahulu ki muuna yoo meeto ahae asamba kupepwa aabone. Mwana mulena ataluseza musizana kuli naa sike alukuluha mwa pilu yahae kufitela aka mulukulula mwa mazoho a musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi yoo. Kacwalo Rapunzelu afelelwa ki sabo ni kulemuha kuli cwale ukona kubaleha mwa mazoho a musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi yoo. Musizana ali, “Nikatabela kuya ni mina kono hanizibi mwa kutulukela kalani ye. Cwale momutela kwanu mutahange ni taulo ya ndendemela kuli nitoluka fateñi matulukelo.”

text.S1: They agreed that he should come to her every evening, for the old woman came by day. The enchantress remarked nothing of this, until once Rapunzel said to her, "Tell me, mother, how it happens that you are so much heavier for me to draw up than the young King's son—he comes this evening." "Ah! you wicked brat," cried the enchantress "What do I hear you say! I thought I had separated you from all evil in the world, and now you have yet deceived me." In her anger she clutched Rapunzel's beautiful braids, wrapped them twice round her left hand, seized a pair of scissors with the right, and snip, snip, they were cut off, and the lovely braids lay on the ground. And she was so pitiless that she took poor Rapunzel into a desert where she had to live in great grief and misery.
text.S2: Both of them agreed that the Prince should be visiting her every evening because the old woman would visit her during day time. The vicious sinful jugglery woman was not aware of what was happening until one day when Rapunzel asked her, “Mom kindly tell me! Why do you weigh more whenever I pull you up than the Prince who will visit me this evening?” “Oho! You are a cruel little girl,” yelled the vicious sinful jugglery woman. “What do I hear you are telling me? I thought that I isolated you from bad things of this world, but now you have betrayed me.” As the vicious sinful jugglery woman is now furious, she grabbed Rapunzel’s dredlocked hair and tied it on her left hand, got a pair of scissors in her right hand and started cutting it short. The beautiful hair lay on the ground. The old woman did not feel mercy on Rapunzel but took her to a desert where she was left to live in pain and more suffering.
text.T1: Ba lumelelana kuli uka mupotelanga manzibuana ni manzibuana, bakeñisa kuli musali muhulu natahanga musihali. Musali wa mabibo nasika lemuha nihaiba hanyinyani ka zeo neli ezahalile, konji foo Rapunzelu hato bulela kuli, "hamuni bulelele, ima, kuli kutaha cwani kuli munani ni bukiti hahulu hani mi hoha kufitela mwana mulena wa muuna--watahanga manzibuana." "Haa! Wena ka mbwitamamina kakanani ni lunya," [A-Z]wae huweleza musali wamabibo, "Niutwile likamani zeubulezi? neni hupula kuli niku kauhanyize kwa lunya lwa lifasi, kono fa uni betekile." Kae bunyemi a nyapa milili ya Rapunzelu, aitama yona kwa lizoho la nzohoto, aswala sikele kwa lizoho la silyo mi kalalala.... kalala....milili ya kutiwa, mi milili yeminde yalobala fafasi. Mi naezize ka lunya luli kuli aisa Rapunzelu wakunyanda mwa lihalaupa moo naizo nyandela ni ku sukuluka.
text.T2: Balumelelana kuli atahange ku musizana zazi ni zazi manzibuana bakeñisa kuli musali-muhulu yena naa tahanga musihali. Musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi naasika lemuha seseñwi ka zene liezahalile, konji foo Rapunzelu hatobulela ali, “Hamuni bulelele, ima, kanti kutaha cwañi kuli mina muna ni bukiti hahulu hanimihoha kufita Nabi, yataha manzibuana woo?” "Haa! Wena ka mbwitamamina kakana ni lunya,” kwahuwa musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi. “Niutwa likamañi zeu bulela? Nahupula kuli niku kauhanyize kwa lunya lwa lifasi, kono kauni beteka” Kabunyemi bwahae, afwañata milili yeotilwe ya Rapunzelu, aitama yona kwa lizoho la nzohoto, aswala sikele kwa lizoho la silyo mi akala kui pumaka ni kuikuta. Milili yeminde yalobala fafasi. Mi naa sikautwela Rapunzelu makeke, ki hamuisa mwa lihalaupa moo naizo pila ka manyando ni kusukuluka.

text.S1: On the same day, howeagreed thatagver, that she cast out Rapunzel, the enchantress fastened the braids of hair which she had cut off to the hook of the window, and when the King's son came and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel,  Let down your hair," she let Rapunzel’s hair down. The King's son ascended, but he did not find the dearest Rapunzel above, but the evil enchantress, who gazed at him with wicked and venomous looks. "Aha!" she cried mockingly, "You would find my dearest, but the beautiful bird sits no longer singing in the nest; the cat has got it. Rapunzel is gone; you will never see her again."
text.S2: However, the same day which Rapunzel was thrown into the wilderness, the vicious sinful jugglery woman tied the hair which she cut off from the girl’s head on the hook that was connected to the window. When the Prince came to call out the girl’s name as usual, “Rapunzel! Rapunzel! Drop your dredlocked hair to me.” The old woman dropped Rapunzel’s hair. Then Prince ascended the tower and unfortunately, he did not meet his beloved Rapunzel in the tower, only the vicious sinful jugglery woman who gazed at him with cruel scaring eyes. “Aah!” she shouted mockingly. “You used to meet my beloved daughter, but the good bird is no longer staying in this nest singing beautiful songs as it has been taken away by a cat. Lapunzel is gone and you will not meet her anymore.”
text.T1: Mwa zazi leliswana, nihakuli cwalo, leo nayubekile Rapunzelu, musali wa muloi atamelela milili yeo na kutile kwa toho ya Rapunzelu kwa lihaulo, mimiwana mulena wa muuna hataha ni kuto huwa, "Rapunzelu, Rapunzelu, posa milili yahao fafasi," Musali aposa milili ya Rapunzelu fafasi. Mwana mulena apahama, kono nasika fumana Rapunzelu ya lateha mwa halimu, kono ayo fumana musali wa mabibo amaswe, yoo utalima ka meeto ahae amaswe luli Ahaa!" Aibulelela ka lishano, "neufumananga mwanaka ya lateha, kono kanyunywani kakande akasa ina mwateni moo, kaze ikashimbile, mi niwena ikaku punyaka meeto. Rapunzelu uile; hausana ku mubona hape."
text.T2: Nihakulicwalo ka lizazi leliswana, lewo naa yumbile Rapunzelu, musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi atamelela milili yeotilwe yanaa kutile kwa toho ya Rapunzelu kwa kashuto ka lihaulo, mi nabi hataha kutohuwa ali, “Rapunzelu! Rapunzelu! Poseza milili yahao fafasi.” Musali aposeza milili ya Rapunzelu fafasi.  Nabi apahama, kabumai naa sikafumana Rapunzelu yalateha mwahalimu konji musali wa mabibo amaswe a sibi yoo amutalima ka meeto ahae abuhali ni lunya luli. “Ahaa!” Ahuwa ka lishano. “Neu fumananga mwanaka yalateha, kono kanyunywani kakande hakasa ina mwateñi moo kanze kaopela mwa siyaleto. Kaze ikaangile mi ni wena ikaku punyaka meeto. Rapunzelu uile, hausana ku mubona hape.”

text.S1: The King's son was beside himself with pain, and in his despair he tower. He escaped with his life, in the forest ate nothing, but roots and berries lament and and weep over the loss of his dearest love. Thus he roamed about in misery for some years, and at length came to the desert where Rapunzel lived in wretchedness. He heard a voice, and it seemed so familiar that he wept going towards it, and when he approached, Rapunzel knew him and fell to her knees and wept. He led her to his Kingdom where hereceived, and they lived for a long time afterwards, happy and content.
text.S2: The Prince lived with depression and in pain at heart, as a result he jumped off the tower. He escaped with his life. He wondered around in the bush without food to eat apart from roots and fruits again there was nothing he could do only crying for missing his loved one. He wondered for few years and finally he reached a desert where Rapunzel was living in difficulties. He heard a familiar voice and followed the direction where it was coming from. As he was approaching the location, Rapunzel recognized him, she fell down on her knees and started crying. Prince took the girl to his palace where they were well welcomed happily and lived together for a long time in happiness and at peace.
text.T1: Mwana mulena autwa hahulu butuku pilu, mi mwa ñalelwa yahae aikwisa kuzwa kwa njongonjongo. Aipulusa, ayambaela mwa mushitu kusina sakuca, kwanda mibisi no litolwana, mi nakusina seo naeza kwanda kulila Kabaka la kulatehelwa ki wa lilato wahae. Kona kuli ayambaela falilimo nyana, miemi mafelelezo ato punyeza mwa lihalaupa moo Rapunzelu na pila mwa manyando. Autwa linzwi, leo neli utwahala kuzibahala, mi aya alila kulatelela linzwi. Hasa atumezi, Rapunzelu amuziba mi akubama fafasi kusituwa sililo. Aisa musizana kwa muleneñi ili koo naailo amuhelwa ka tabo luli, mi bapila nako yetelele hamoho, batabile ni kuiketa.
text.T2: Nabi apila inge autwa hahulu butuku kwa pilu, mi mwa ñalelwa yahae atula fa kalani. Abaleha ni bupilo bwahae cwalo. Ayambayela mwa mushitu cwalo kusina sakuca kwandaa mibisi ni litolwana, mi nekusina sewo naeza kwanda kulila kulatehelwa ki mulatiwa wahae. Ayambayela mwa lilimo-nyana, kono kwamafelelezo atopunyeza mwa lihalaupa moo Rapunzelu naapila mwa manyando. Autwa linzwi lene liutwahala kuzibahala mi alatelela kone lizwelela. Hase aatumezi, Rapunzelu amuziba mi akubama fafasi ni kusituwa sililo. Aisa musizana kwa muleneñi wahae ili koo naailo amuhelwa ka tabo luli mi bayopila nako yetelele hamoho inge batabile ni kabuiketo.
